change.title: pr-37038-flat
change.description: Add Groups resource type and scopes to authorization schema
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: V2 canManage() is granted by VIEW on all groups, so view-only admins can create and re-parent groups
findings.body: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (lines 65-71) returns true when the caller holds VIEW or MANAGE on the all-groups resource (`hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`, line 70). The no-argument requireManage() is the only guard on POST /groups (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/GroupsResource.java:180-181). That handler also calls realm.moveGroup(child, null) for an existing group id (GroupsResource.java:191-198). Before this PR, V2 used the base GroupPermissions.canManage(), which checks only MANAGE_USERS (GroupPermissions.java:273-276). MgmtPermissionsV2.groups() (MgmtPermissionsV2.java:57-62) is the change that routes V2 to the new class. So an admin with only a `view` permission on the Groups resource can now create top-level groups and move any existing subgroup to the top level. No test covers this: testManageAllGroups grants MANAGE only (GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java:158-160). The Javadoc at GroupPermissionEvaluator.java:72-77 documents the VIEW rule, but it contradicts canManage(GroupModel) (MANAGE only) and UserPermissionsV2.canManage(user) (MANAGE only). Fix: make V2 canManage() check MANAGE only, correct the Javadoc, and add a test where a VIEW-only admin gets 403 on POST /groups.

findings.title: V2 getGroupIdsWithViewPermission collects resource IDs, not group IDs, so group-scoped view grants never restrict the user listing
findings.body: (a) Per-group resources are created in AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource with the group ID as name and no type (server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:118-121). V1 sets type 'Group' (GroupPermissions.java:117). V2 iterates findByType(server, 'Groups') (line 121). That probably matches only the type resource, not the per-group resources. (b) Line 123 adds groupResource.getId(), the internal resource ID, not the group ID. (c) Line 122 passes that same internal ID to hasPermission(), which looks resources up by name (line 141). The lookup never finds the group resource, so it falls back to the all-groups resource (lines 143-149). The result is a set of IDs that match no group. Consequences: UsersResource.searchForUser does not set the GROUPS attribute (UsersResource.java:448-453), so the listing is not restricted and is paged before the per-user filter at UsersResource.java:460. The count endpoints call getUsersCount(..., groupIds), which returns 0 for an empty set (model/jpa/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/jpa/JpaUserProvider.java:634-637). A caller with VIEW_MEMBERS on a group therefore gets short or empty pages and a count that does not match the list. If the all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS grant applies, the bogus ID is put into GROUPS and the list is empty. No error is raised. Fix: collect and look up by resource name (the group ID), and make the iteration reach the per-group resources (for example, set a type in getOrCreateResource, or find them another way). The typing premise in (a) is the part I could not fully confirm; the ID mismatch in (b) and (c) holds either way.

findings.title: testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers passes even though the GROUPS restriction is broken
findings.body: With no group IDs found (see the previous finding), the query is unrestricted. The per-user filter in UsersResource.toRepresentation (UsersResource.java:460) still returns alice, so the assertion passes. The test asserts only the list, not the count endpoint or pagination, so it does not exercise the path its name describes. Add a count assertion (users().count()) or a paged search (first=0, max=1) to the same setup. There is also no coverage for VIEW-only creation of top-level groups (see the blocker).

findings.title: Subgroup listing in V2 may hide subgroups that have their own permission resource, even when all-groups VIEW applies
findings.body: getSubGroups now filters with auth.groups()::canView (line 179). For V2 that is GroupPermissionsV2.canView(group) (GroupPermissionsV2.java:55-62), which calls hasPermission(group.getId()). The all-groups fallback (GroupPermissionsV2.java:141-150) runs only when the subgroup has no resource of its own. Before this change, an admin with all-groups VIEW saw every subgroup through canViewGlobal. Now a subgroup that has its own permission entry is hidden from that admin in this listing, while GET /groups/{id} (GroupResource.java:101) uses the same check. Is it intended that a per-group resource shadows the all-groups grant? UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission has the same shape (UserPermissionsV2.java:105-114). If it is intended, no change is needed; if not, the shadowing needs a fix in hasPermission.

findings.title: Javadoc says getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns a Stream, but it returns a Set
findings.body: The @return tag at line 145 says 'Stream of IDs of groups with view permission', but the method (line 147) returns Set<String>, and the implementations return a Set (GroupPermissions.java:298, GroupPermissionsV2.java:106). Change the tag to 'Set of IDs of groups with view permission'.

contracts.action: POST /groups (addTopLevelGroup) and the rep.getId() re-parent branch call auth.groups().requireManage(), which now resolves to GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()
contracts.equivalent_path: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissions.java:273-276 (V1 canManage: MANAGE_USERS role only; this was the V2 behaviour before the PR)
contracts.before_after: Before: V2 canManage() = MANAGE_USERS role only. After: also true when the caller holds VIEW on the all-groups resource (GroupPermissionsV2.java:70).
contracts.visible_effect: A view-only admin can create top-level groups and move an existing subgroup to the top level (GroupsResource.java:191-198).
contracts.failure_mode: Silent over-grant: the request succeeds with no error or log.

contracts.action: GET /users search and count call auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() and set the GROUPS session attribute
contracts.equivalent_path: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissions.java:298-320 (V1: findByType 'Group', strips the 'group.resource.' prefix to get the group ID)
contracts.before_after: Before: V2 inherited the V1 method, which never matches V2 resource names, so it also returned nothing. After: the V2 override returns resource UUIDs and checks by UUID, so it still returns no group IDs. The new code does not restore group-scoped restriction.
contracts.visible_effect: Users granted only VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS on a group are missing from listings and counts. A list can be unrestricted and paged before filtering, while the count returns 0 (JpaUserProvider.java:634-637). With an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS grant, the GROUPS attribute can hold a bogus ID and the list is empty.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent wrong result: short or empty pages and a count that does not match the list. No error is raised. The per-user filter (UsersResource.java:460) keeps unauthorised users out, so this is not a data leak.

contracts.action: UsersResource.searchForUser drops the second .filter(usersEvaluator::canView) before toRepresentation
contracts.before_after: Before: the filter ran twice. After: once, in toRepresentation. The same users are returned.
contracts.failure_mode: None: the authorisation filter still runs on every returned user.

contracts.action: BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser calls getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() without the canView guard
contracts.before_after: Before: the call ran only when canView() was false. After: it always runs, but the V2 override returns an empty set when canView() is true, so the GROUPS attribute is not set in either case.
contracts.visible_effect: None beyond the group-ID issue in the previous contract.
contracts.failure_mode: Same as the UsersResource contract above.

contracts.action: GET /groups/{id}/children filters subgroups with auth.groups()::canView, replacing canViewGlobal || canView(g)
contracts.before_after: Before: V2 canViewGlobal (all-groups VIEW) passed every subgroup. After: each subgroup is checked against its own resource when one exists; the all-groups fallback runs only when it does not.
contracts.visible_effect: A subgroup that has its own permission resource can be hidden from an admin whose only grant is all-groups VIEW.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent omission from the listing; no error.
contracts.open_question: Is it intended that a per-group permission resource shadows the all-groups grant, as UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission does for users?

contracts.action: GroupPermissions.requireViewMembers and canViewMembers now accept MANAGE_MEMBERS
contracts.before_after: Before: requireViewMembers accepted MANAGE_MEMBERS through getGroupsWithViewPermission(group), while canViewMembers accepted only VIEW_MEMBERS. After: both accept either scope, and the canView() and canManage() bypasses are kept.
contracts.visible_effect: getAccess().viewMembers is true for MANAGE_MEMBERS holders, as the Javadoc describes.

contracts.action: AdminPermissions.registerListener registers its ProviderEventListener only when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled
contracts.before_after: Before: always registered, with the feature checked inside onEvent. After: the feature is checked once at registration.
contracts.visible_effect: None, provided feature flags are fixed at startup.

contracts.action: ApiUtil.handleCreatedResponse closes the response via try-with-resources
contracts.before_after: Before: response.close() ran only on the success path. After: the response is also closed when the 201 assertion fails.
contracts.failure_mode: None. Callers that close the response again are unaffected, since close is idempotent.

summary:
**Batch 1 of 1.** test

**Batch 1 of 1, retry.** Blocker: V2 GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() is also granted by VIEW on all groups (GroupPermissionsV2.java:65-71). GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup calls the no-argument requireManage() (GroupsResource.java:181), and the re-parent branch calls moveGroup (lines 191-198). So a view-only V2 admin can create top-level groups and move subgroups to the top level, and no test covers it. Fix: check MANAGE only and correct the Javadoc. Fix-level: V2 getGroupIdsWithViewPermission collects resource UUIDs and looks them up by name, so group-scoped view-members grants never restrict the user listing or count; results are silently wrong, though the per-user filter still prevents a leak. Also a consider-level test gap, a subgroup-listing shadowing question, and a Javadoc Stream/Set mismatch. The other removed symbols have no remaining references. Compile-sensitive edits (GroupResource.addChild definite assignment, MgmtPermissionsV2.groups() signature) check out. No ADR files were found at the head snapshot (docs/adr/ does not exist). Nothing was built or run.
